title: Expect a (Damp) Full House at IMSA’s Petit Le Mans Finale

body_markdown:
One of the longest seasons in all of sports winds up on Saturday with the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship finale at Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta—the 10-hour Motul Petit Le Mans.


The fight for the 2026 championship in all four classes, which began January 24-25 with the Rolex 24 Hours at Daytona, comes down to this last race, though in the top class, GTP, the No. 31 Whelen-sponsored Cadillac V-Series.R holds a comfortable lead, both for the manufacturer’s championship and the individual driver’s championship.


For Cadillac to win the overall manufacturer crown, just one of the three Cadillacs entered has to start the race, so consider that a lock. For the driver’s championship, though, Jack Aitken’s No. 31[Action Express](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/cadillac-corvette-earn-first-wins-of-26-on-the-streets-of-detroit/) car has to finish ninth or better. And since there are 11 cars in the class, that’s pretty close to being a lock, too, though Aitken isn’t ready to start counting his chickens. Second-place driver Lauren Heinrich, who will be in the No. 7 Penske Porsche 963, will have to win the race overall to have a chance at taking the title from Aitken.


So for Aitken, then, it sounds like business as usual at a track he likes. “We’ve done well there over the last few years, and particularly last year,” he said via a Zoom call earlier this week. “We’re pretty confident we can come in and have a decent car off the bat. My goal is to try and have a great qualifying. And hopefully that means that we could go into the race worry-free and just enjoy it and race for the win.”


[Cameron Neveu](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/cameron-neveu/)


That’s especially important for[Gary Nelson](https://www.hagerty.com/media/people/meet-gary-nelson-who-made-nascar-safe/) , team manager at Action Express. Nelson, the former NASCAR Daytona 500-winning crew chief and one-time head of NASCAR’s research and development department, has long made it clear that at this point in his career, “I’m just running for the trophies,” as he said in a previous interview. The team won the[2025 Petit Le Mans.](https://www.hagerty.com/media/motorsports/four-season-championships-up-for-grabs-in-saturdays-petit-le-mans-sports-car-race/)


“We’ve done a very good job over the last year, I think, both in terms of putting a fast car out there and having pretty clean, efficient, well-called races,” Aitken said. “And we do that by weighing up risk by planning out and prepping a lot of the stuff that we do. Every professional, whether it’s the guys making the calls on the pit wall, or me or Earl \[Bamber\] or Frederik \[Vesti\] in the car, puts a lot of effort into trying to calibrate that risk/reward level and kind of get it right.”


[Eddy Eckart](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/eeckarthagerty-com/)


Certainly, in that respect, Aitken’s competition is all of the other 10 cars in the GTP class, but specifically Heinrich in the No. 7 Porsche, which he will share this weekend with Felipe Nasr and Julien Andlauer; that trio won this year’s Rolex 24 at Daytona and Mobil 1 Twelve Hours at Sebring races. Porsche and Penske will return in 2027 for a fifth IMSA season with the 963 race car, and possibly their last.


The championship battle is closer in the other three classes going into Petit. In Le Mans Prototype 2, where all the cars run an Oreca chassis and identical V-8 engines, the driver duo of Jeremy Clarke and Tom Dillman, driving for InterEuropol, lead by just four points over Alex Quinn in the CrowdStrike Racing car.


Mercedes-AMG teammates Philip Ellis and Russell Ward, driving for Winward Racing, have a six-point lead in GT Daytona over Turner Motorsport BMW teammates Robby Foley and Patrick Gallagher.


[Eddy Eckart](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/eeckarthagerty-com/)


And in GTD Pro—which utilizes the same production-based cars as GTD but allows for a professional driver lineup instead of Pro-Am combinations—the points lead is held by Chevrolet Corvette Racing by Pratt Miller Motorsports teammates Tommy Milner and Nicky Catsburg, who have a reasonably comfortable lead of 47 points over Paul Miller BMW teammates Connor de Phillippi and Neil Verhagen.


Tommy Milner at the pit box of the #4 Corvette


Lumen Digital Agency


Driver Milner, on the same Zoom call as Cadillac’s Aitken, said that “For us, it’s as we’ve approached all the other races this year. Obviously we need to score good points, no matter what. I know there are lots of points possibilities and things like that we won’t bother ourselves with at this point. They won’t matter until the race gets going.


“But yeah, we’ve had a good year so far,” Milner said. “Some ups and some downs, but obviously great to be P1 going into the last race.” Nico Varrone re-joins Milner and Catsburg as the third driver, required for the longest races.


A capacity field of 54 cars has entered—11 in GTP, 11 in LMP2, 18 in GTD and 14 in GTD Pro—which means a lot of traffic on the tight 12-turn, 2.54-mile road course. Since many other series have concluded their seasons, marquee-level guest drivers will be making an appearance at Petit, including open-wheel racers Colton Herta, Scott Dixon, Kyle Kirkwood, and Alex Palou, as well as WEC regulars Sebastien Bourdais and Kevin Magnussen.


At this writing, the weather forecast calls for an 87 percent chance of rain, which could make for an especially interesting race. Yes, the teams do have rain tires, and the cars have windshield wipers.


The 2026 Petit Le Mans takes the green flag at noon ET on Saturday, with the first three hours televised on NBC, then NBCSN assumes coverage and goes to the 10 p.m. checkered flag. The race will also stream on Peacock, and the radio broadcast is available at IMSA.com.
